Impact with terrain for reasons that could not be determined because the airplane was not recovered due to the inaccessible nature of the accident site.

Contributing to the accident were the exceedance of specified engine inspection intervals and the unsuitable forced landing location.

The pilot’s in-flight loss of control due to the structural failure of a wing fitting and separation of the outboard wing section. Also causal were the inadequate wing fitting inspections, which failed to detect the initial corrosion and crack before it resulted in failure of the wing fitting lug.

The pilot’s failure to maintain an adequate airspeed during landing, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall.
The loss of lift while on final approach which resulted in a hard off-airport landing.
Pilot incapacitation shortly after takeoff for unknown reasons.

The airplane’s collision with a deer on the runway during landing.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control in gusty wind conditions during landing, which resulted in a runway excursion and collision with terrain.
The failure of the left main landing gear due to the lack of lubrication.
The pilot’s failure to maintain airplane control during the takeoff.
